entities.summary: Pharnabazus III was a Persian satrap who played a pivotal role in the conquest of Anatolia by Alexander the Great. As the son of Artabazos II, Pharnabazus III was appointed as the satrap of Lydia, a region crucial to the Persian Empire's control over Asia Minor. His strategic position allowed him to resist Alexander's advances, but ultimately, he was forced to surrender to the Macedonian king. This event had significant consequences for the region, as it led to the spread of Greek culture and the establishment of the Hellenistic period in Asia Minor. The legacy of Pharnabazus III can be seen in the architectural and cultural achievements of the Hellenistic period, which continued to shape the region for centuries to come. The city of Ephesus, once a thriving metropolis under Pharnabazus III's rule, became a major center of Greek culture and learning during the Hellenistic period. The statue of Pharnabazus III is said to have been erected in the city of Pergamon, a testament to his enduring legacy.
